messages:
incident-bot: P0 page to #incidents: 
  - Summary: Tier-routing cascade detected — requests intended for hosted pool are being routed into Dedicated pools in us-west1 causing capacity pressure + region fallback. Multiple customers reporting elevated latency and errors. Pager: @michelle_oncall, @leo_ops

michelle_oncall: Got the page, looking. TL;DR — huge spike of requests landing in dedicated pool + model mismatch.

leo_ops: Observed sustained 80% CPU on dedicated-pool-usw1-4 and rising queue depth. KPIs: latency p95 -> 3.8s, error rate 5% -> 18% on /v1/generate for some tenants.

maya_prod: Affected customers: crmco and searchly — both on hosted plan. They see 502s and token failures. Customer support flagged 3 active incidents.

sanjay_eng: I pulled recent routing-policy commits — there was a small hotfix merged 27m ago to routing-config that adjusted fallback weights. Diff shows an accidental flip of the capacity_tier precedence key:

```
# before
priority:
  capacity_tier:
    - hosted
    - dedicated
# after (bad)
priority:
  capacity_tier:
    - dedicated
    - hosted
```

sanjay_eng: That change would make dedicated preferred for some routes if both are compatible -> explains the misroute. Also I see a tag mismatch: model_variant_tag on dedicated pool is accepting anything with tag 'stable' because of a missing strict match.

evans_infra: Netops telemetry shows cross-region fallback chatter: us-east1 tried to fallback to us-west1 due to a transient kube autoscaler blip, but because dedicated now preferred the chain closed into a loop where hosted traffic spilled into dedicated, then capacity loss triggered region fallback, which bounced back.

alice_sre: Paging timeline attached in logs; initial config change deploy @1766662600, error detection at 1766664280, page at 1766664321.

michelle_oncall: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Prevent new misroutes by flip override to pin routes to hosted 2) Quarantine dedicated pool variant acceptance to strict tag match 3) Roll back commit if needed. Who can apply the policy override?

sanjay_eng: I can push an override. Pushing temporary policy: `rctl routing override set --match 'customer.plan: hosted' --force-target=hosted --ttl=30m`

netops-bot: Command accepted. Override applied in control-plane (id: ov-1766664335).

leo_ops: Confirming traffic — within 60s I'm seeing decrease in requests to dedicated-pool-usw1-4. Queue depth dropping. Latency trending down.

maya_prod: Customer errors decreasing. CRMCO reports latency back to normal for their API calls. Marking customer-facing incident as mitigated.

evans_infra: While override is helping, dedicated pool still has queued connections for long-running inflight requests. We should tighten variant acceptance: `kubectl -n inference patch configmap pool-dedicated-usw1 --type merge -p '{"data": {"allowed_variant_tags": "stable|pinned"}}'`

sanjay_eng: Applying config patch now.

netops-bot: Patch applied to configmap pool-dedicated-usw1 at 1766664442. Reconcile in progress.

leo_ops: Reconcile shows dedicated pool now rejecting requests with variant_tag != pinned/stable. Inflight bad-model calls are failing gracefully with 429; frontends are rerouting to hosted as per override.

michelle_oncall: Good. I'm going to hand off monitoring/war room to @sanjay_eng. I'll stay on slack for 15m. If anything regresses, page me.

michelle_oncall: Handoff: active mitigations — control-plane override (ov-1766664335), dedicated pool tag restriction applied, incident owner -> leo_ops, follow-up PM -> maya_prod, postmortem owner -> sanjay_eng.

sanjay_eng: Taking over. I'll coordinate rollback of the bad config change after we confirm full stabilization. Also opening a temporary canary that forces a small fraction (1%) to go through prior logic to validate no silent regressions.

netops-bot: Canary traffic started (canary-id: c-1766664500) routed to hosted path. No errors observed in 5m window.

leo_ops: All primary KPIs back to baseline. p95 < 400ms, error rate < 0.5% across impacted tenants. Dedicated pool CPU normalized to 28%.

maya_prod: Notifying customers: CRMCO and Searchly updated via support with status "mitigated; ongoing monitoring".

michelle_oncall: Marking incident as 'under control' at 1766664620. Please complete post-incident ticket with timeline and root cause.

alice_sre: Root cause hypothesis: a faulty merge changed capacity_tier precedence in routing policy, combined with lax variant-tag enforcement on dedicated pools, produced cross-tier preference inversion. That caused hosted traffic to be preferred to route into dedicated pools; subsequent autoscaler reactions created region fallbacks and a short feedback loop.

leo_ops: Immediate action items for next 24h: 1) revert the routing-config commit (or fix precedence key) 2) add CI check for capacity_tier precedence diffs 3) enforce strict tag matching on pool config as default 4) run synthetic end-to-end tests for route precedence.

sanjay_eng: I've opened PR #routing-1767 to revert the bad change and added a unit test. ETA for merge + deploy: 2h.

michelle_oncall: Great. Final note for pager: Incident resolved for paging escalation; will keep watch for 2h and then close. Postmortem owner @sanjay_eng. If anyone has logs/screenshots to add, append here.

leo_ops: Adding a quick log excerpt showing the misroute pattern:
```
2026-03-15T12:03:40Z router INFO route_eval tenant=crmco match=capacity_tier=>dedicated selected_pool=dedicated-usw1-4 variant_tag=unstable
2026-03-15T12:03:41Z dedicated-usw1-4 WARN queue_depth=112 cpu=92% inflight_tokens=840
2026-03-15T12:04:02Z router INFO fallback region=us-west1 -> us-east1 due_to=capacity_shortage
```
maya_prod: I'll file the customer follow-up email template and KG article for "temporary routing impact".

michelle_oncall: Closing active page at 1766664899. Leave thread for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone. :bow:
